text: A flame cultivated by Xiao Xiao from his own pure bloodline, wieldable only by true descendants of the Zhu Long. It specializes in vanquishing the treacherous and wicked, burning away all that is unclean.

Personally crafted by Bin Long and bestowed upon Xiao Xiao, this armor bears carvings of the Vermillion Bird, its battle robes embroidered with the sigil of Zhu Long. Golden winds and sunlit flames swirl about the wearer, capable of dispersing ordinary stray arrows.

One of the Six Great Tiger Tallies of the Long Wall, the Flame Tally represents the mobile reinforcements, embodying the unwavering faith of the countless soldiers who guard the Long Wall. Its bearer holds the authority to summon reinforcements from the defensive line.

A token of Zhu Long's own bloodline, containing the Winds of Magic of the Lore of Life from the southern frontier. Bestowed upon Xiao Xiao by Bin Long upon reaching adulthood, this pendant stabilizes the bloodline and wards off the corruption of Chaos.

Forged by Bin Long himself, blending refined Kun Lan gold with the dark iron of the western frontier, this armor is rough-hewn yet heavy, its beast-face fierce and menacing—only one who wields the power of the Four Symbols may don it into battle.

Guided by the teachings of a secretive alchemist, Xuan Lie forged this power through the trials of the Western Frontier's wars, channeling the dragon veins of the western lands through his own body to unleash the earth's tectonic force, tearing apart enemy formations.
A steed of dragon-blood, its coat pitch black; it travels ten thousand li by day and eight thousand more by night—thus it earned the name Ten Thousand Miles of Mist and Cloud.

A wondrous ancient jade bestowed by the Soaring Dragon. Xuan Lie's pure dragon bloodline readily draws heavenly thunder, and this jade pendant channels and disperses the lightning strikes, tempering his body to make him stronger still.

A divine weapon only those of the Soaring Dragon bloodline can wield, housing within it the spirit of a temple-guarding beast imbued with the power of wind and thunder. Its strikes sweep through enemy ranks like a dragon's lashing tail, scattering thousands.

Hong Ying possesses an uncanny affinity for the Yin winds of magic. His "staff" is the ink-jade flame upon his blade; when he must channel the winds of magic or cut down a target, the ink flame rises and shifts form.
This cloak, light as swan's down, is the symbol of the overseer who commands the "Shadow Crow Guard"—it is also the sole means, besides Yuan Bo himself, of directly commanding the Agate Crowmen.

The Cassia Confidants are divided into three guards, and only the overseer of each guard may hold this token. Hong Ying's "Shadow Crow Guard" bears the duty of gathering intelligence across the realm and carrying out assassinations and arrests—showing this token is as if the Moon Empress herself had arrived.

[Shadowdance] is the Great Moon Luan bestowed upon Hong Ying by the Moon Empress herself. Rumor holds that this bird is the Moon Empress's own phantom; only by hearing its cry can the Black Jade Crow Wardens commune with the Yin wind and transform into the Yue Zhuo.

Legend holds that this mask was carved by the Shadow Dragon itself. Its wearer can not only conceal their presence, but move with the wind upon the battlefield, vanishing into shadow to strike down enemy commanders.

A powerful weapon that Shadowdance brought back from the Moon Empress's residence. Its blade is as bright and clear as the moon, with flowing ink-jade like flame upon it that can easily dispel the magic bound to an opponent's weapon.

The Hairpin of Longing for the Palace is carved from thousand-year-old cassia wood and tempered with shadow magic. When Liu Wang Que followed Yuan Bo to Lustria, Hong Ying solemnly entrusted this hairpin to her; the shadow power within amplifies spells while concealing the caster's presence.

The Golden Feather Robe is woven from moonlit silk gifted by the Moon Empress, reinforced with threads of refined gold, its shawl made from the molted feathers of spirit crows raised by the Cassia Confidants. Woven over the course of a year by the Celestial Weaving Bureau, it is Liu Wang Que's most distinguishing mark of identity.

Liu Wang Que's wisdom foiled a plot by followers of Tzeentch to destroy the Cassia soul, earning great renown. [Shadowdance] brought it to her, plucked from the Moon Empress's garden; legend holds that the Mirror of the Cassia Soul was forged by the Moon Empress's own hands, its back etched with the ancient inscription, "Moonlight shines through a thousand gates, its shadow follows but one." Whoever holds this mirror leaves no enemy hidden.

[Mirror Bloom] and [Shadowdance] are a mated pair of Great Moon Luans, bound to each other for life. Rumor holds them to be part of the Moon Empress's own power; upon hearing the cry of these two birds, the Black Jade Crow Wardens can commune with the Yin Wind and transform into the sacred Yue Zhuo bird.

The Moonlight Edict is the token of office of the Cassia Confidants' deputy chief, and Liu Wang Que's proof of authority to command the organization. On the battlefield, the Moonlight Edict can release a magical barrier to protect its bearer, resonating with the Mirror of the Cassia Soul.

When Hong Ying first established the Cassia Confidants, he personally forged this long saber for Liu Wang Que with ink flame as her weapon of war. Though the deputy chief of the Cassia Confidants is a woman, she is by no means one to be trifled with.

A great shield forged especially for the terracotta commander, its primary material Kun Lan obsidian, its face embossed with the magnificent form of the Dragon God. Utterly indestructible, it can block even the heaviest blows of giant beasts.
Whether arrows, blades, fangs, or claws—the divine dragon statue coiled about the beast-devouring emblem regards all such crude methods of slaughter with utter, bone-deep contempt.
A rare crystal from the peak of Kun Lan, set into Yang Xing's armor, holds within it the power of the Heavenly Way, capable of unleashing deadly magical energy in battle.

The sword of Yang Xing, foremost of the terracotta statues, said to have been forged by the Dragon Emperor's own hand. Its blade is engraved with patterns of the Yang wind, and it shines with dazzling starlight whenever Chaos assails the Long Wall.

The prototypes of these war machines trace back to the prospecting boom of the Golden Age, but as engineers and miners were swallowed by the green tide, they too were buried deep beneath the rubble until recent excavations brought them back into the light. Now, survivors of that terrible calamity mount these refurbished, mass-produced machines to settle the score with the greenskins and ratkin scum.
Thor met the dwarf Gerd when he won a drinking contest. When they fled the dark elves' Black Ark, a storm swept Gerd away, leaving behind only his friend's heirloom runic helm.
This armor was forged by a renowned dwarf master, imbued with a long-lost thunder rune. It not only channels Halfdan's inner thunderous power, but also cleanses the chaos energy surrounding him.

After defeating the bone-crushing giant chieftain in single combat, Halfdan claimed this golden rune from the giant's hoard. Its bearer possesses boundless charisma, compelling others to follow willingly.
When the divine hammer descended wreathed in lightning, it left an ever-lasting lightning scar upon Halfdan's chest. This scar renders Thor's chosen one impervious to blade and arrow alike.
It was this hammer, fallen from the sky, that turned a new page in Halfdan's life. When he grips its haft, he can hear Thor's divine oracle guiding him to overcome all.
The largest and most bloodthirsty of ripperdactyls, their razor-sharp claws can decapitate enemies, and their furious assaults leave scattered entrails and severed limbs in their wake.

Whatever the identity or danger of the foe, Alastar rides his war lion into a charge that would make the Lion God himself proud.

The soft metal, though unable to protect his hard scaly hide, makes his massive frame shine brilliantly, allowing the Saurus warriors following him into the enemy's depths to more easily track his gleaming silhouette and follow the bloody path he carves.

Indestructibility applied to a weapon becomes unbreakable might. This massive hammer, one that would require several Kroxigors to carry, moves in Gu Kahn's hands as fluidly as an extension of his own limbs. A single casual blow can smash warmbloods and their so-called fine armor into a mangled heap of flesh and metal.
Assembled from the most prized trophies of Gu Ke Jia's kills, this thick carapace, capable of withstanding the heat of the Sun Engine, renders shot and arrows as harmless as scratches through a boot.

Sharp, heavy, and imbued with the wild blessing of the beast god Itza, this great axe—polished by a legion of Spirit Skink artisans—is enough to behead a carnosaur with a single blow, no matter how thick its neck.
